# `format-added`

Format added

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `error` in requests, `info` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `format-added` (both directions), `format-added-in-request`, `format-added-in-response` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

A `format` was added to a schema that had none, e.g. a plain string became `format: uuid`.

## Why this default

In requests: clients' existing values may not match the format and are rejected. In responses: clients receive values in a narrower format, which is safe.

## Example

From test case [`format-added`](../../test/cases/format-added/): A format added to a request string.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
          name:
            type: string
+           format: uuid
```

Findings:

- `format-added-in-request` · error · #/components/schemas/Pet

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  format-added: info
```

## How to fix

In requests, validate the format only for new clients, or keep it unformatted.
